claims.nodeLabel: SAF/AAZ - Air Force Declassification & Special Programs
claims.text: The 2014 edition of AFI 16-701 was certified by SAF/AAZ, then Mr. Daniel F. McMillin, with SAF/AAZE as office of primary responsibility.

claims.nodeLabel: SAF/AAZ - Air Force Declassification & Special Programs
claims.text: Para. 2.1.2.4 directs SAF/AAZ to 'establish a declassification program and ensure that necessary resources are applied to the review of information to ensure it is neither classified for longer than necessary nor declassified prematurely in accordance with the file series exemption'.

claims.nodeLabel: SAF/AAZ - Air Force Declassification & Special Programs
claims.text: SAF/AAZ serves as Designated Accreditation Authority for all SAP information systems and as access approval authority for all SAPs, approving waivers for SAP access; both authorities may be delegated only in writing and must be revalidated annually.

claims.nodeLabel: SAF/AAZ - Air Force Declassification & Special Programs
claims.text: AFI 16-701 (18 February 2014, 48 pages) identifies SAF/AAZ as 'the Secretary of the Air Force, Security, Counterintelligence, and Special Program Oversight' and requires all supplements to the instruction to be routed to SAF/AAZ for coordination before certification and approval.

claims.nodeLabel: SAF/AAZ - Air Force Declassification & Special Programs
claims.text: Para. 2.1 assigns the Director, Security and Special Program Oversight (SAF/AAZ) to serve as principal advisor to SAF/AA for SAPs and as Director, AF SAPCO, developing SAP policy and directing, administering and overseeing the SAP security programme.

a.label: SAF/AAZ - Air Force Declassification & Special Programs

b.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)

edges.label: Air Force SAP Central Office subordinate to DoD SAPCO approval authority
edges.note: SAF/AAZ is the Air Force Special Access Program Central Office. Under AFPD 16-7 it administers Air Force SAPs on behalf of the Secretary of the Air Force while release of SAP material outside the department requires DoD SAPCO approval, placing SAF/AAZ inside the OSD-level special access architecture.

a.label: SAF/AAZ - Air Force Declassification & Special Programs

edges.label: Air Force SAP directive bars congressional briefings without SAPCO approval
edges.note: Air Force Policy Directive 16-7, 'Special Access Programs,' 29 December 2010, states: 'It is strictly forbidden for any employee of the Air Force or any appropriately accessed organization or company to brief or provide SAP material to any Congressional Member or staff without DoD SAPCO approval. Additionally, the Director, SAF/AAZ will be kept informed of any interaction with Congress.' This is the documented mechanism behind the recurring complaint that SAP-compartmented material cannot reach non-HASC/HAC-D members.
